about: The constants the tract's acoustics take -- air's, the walls', the losses' and the static ducts' sizes -- each with where it comes from: measured (air; the walls' tissue; printed replicas' bandwidths and flows) or chosen near what was measured, and by whom (the owner, 16 November 2026: "Document the sources of tract measurements and place those measurements in config files as constants, similar to our approach to measurements of woodwind instruments"). build.rs writes each `rust` name as a Rust constant with its `value` exactly as written here, into the module each group names (`modules`: src/constants.rs, src/v24/constants.rs, src/tube.rs, src/v24/tube.rs): so a change here is a change to the sound, and the values are VocalTractLab's own, to which the port is held sample by sample (docs/VOCAL_TRACT.md). The living tracts the engine is held to are in voices/measured-tracts.json; the radiation's categories in acoustics/radiation.json.

air.about: Air as VocalTractLab takes it (its Constants.h: "Physical constants according to Flanagan (1965)": J. L. Flanagan 1965, Speech Analysis, Synthesis and Perception, Springer), CGS units; 2.3's port, 2.4's network and the passive core alike.

criticalReynolds.about: Where a constriction's flow turns turbulent and its noise sources sound (VocalTractLab 2.3's Constants.h; 2.4's noise takes its own thresholds, src/v24/tds.rs).

walls.about: The tract's walls as each section's mass, damping and stiffness per unit of its wall's area (2.4's network and the passive core's wall branches: src/v24/tds.rs, src/v24/passive.rs). VocalTractLab 2.4's values (Constants.cpp), one set for every speaker. They lie within what K. Ishizaka, J. C. French & J. L. Flanagan measured on living tissue (1975, "Direct determination of vocal tract wall impedance", IEEE Trans. ASSP 23(4), 370-373, as VocalTractLab 2.3's Tube.cpp lists their three sites, `measured`; the paper itself not yet to hand: research/SOURCES_TO_FETCH.md); Fant 1972 found women's walls lighter than men's (voices/measured-tracts.json), which one set does not follow.

measured.as: VocalTractLab 2.3's Tube.cpp, commented out beside its own: "Data for the relaxed cheeck", "Data for the tense-cheeck", "Data for the neck"

tissues.about: The walls' tissue a renderer may ask of the passive core by name (tissue=NAME: PassiveModel::take_switches, tissue_factors), or by a number, the walls' own resonance over 2.4's: a resonance r raised by lighter walls, their mass and damping each 1/r^2 of 2.4's, so that the walls' own resonance keeps its width (damping over mass), their stiffness kept. None asked, 2.4's walls for every speaker. Each speaker's walls named in voices/speakers.json (`walls`); a blended body's resonance its speakers' weighed by the blend (native/vocaltract/sing-score.mjs --tissue speaker). Every wall of the tract takes it, the nose's and the trachea's with the pharynx's and the mouth's, as 2.4 gives them one wall.

men.about: 2.4's walls: the lips closed, their resonance 159 to 200 Hz on the three speakers and 113 Hz wide, within men's measured 150 to 200 Hz in frequency and at the top of the widths measured (Fant 1972, Fujimura & Lindqvist 1971, Hanna, Smith & Wolfe 2016: research/VOCALWIND_BOUNDARY_LAYER.md, "Against living tracts")

women.about: G. Fant 1972, "Vocal tract wall effects, losses, and resonance bandwidths", STL-QPSR 13(2-3), 28-52, page 47: his women's walls' term in the first bandwidth 30% larger than his men's, "i.e. by a 14% higher equivalent F_W" -- the closed tract's resonance, the walls' mass against the tract's air -- set by him to his two women's measured bandwidths (Fujimura & Lindqvist's sweep tones, glottis closed): women's walls lighter, "the mass of the surrounding wall is significantly smaller for females than for males" (O. Fujimura & J. Lindqvist 1971, JASA 49(2B), 541-558).

rigid.about: For checks against printed tracts with hard walls (Birkholz, Blandin & Kürbis 2023; voices/measured-tracts.json): the walls 10^12 times 2.4's mass, so that they move a part in 10^12 of a living wall's -- held rigid without a change to the step.

walls23.about: VocalTractLab 2.3's walls (its Tube.cpp, the port's src/tube.rs): "I gave the wall a higher resistance than proposed in the literature. With a lower resistance, F1 increases very strongly (making it hard to get, e.g., a good /u/). The wall stiffness mainly controls how long a voicebar lasts in the closure phase of a plosive. It has little effect on the F1 damping." (P. Birkholz, its comment).

losses.about: The viscous resistance per unit length, the larger of two power laws of a section's area A (P. Birkholz & P. Häsner 2026, "Viscous and kinetic losses in transmission-line models of the vocal tract", IEEE Access, doi:10.1109/ACCESS.2026.3728208, Eq. 14: R' = max{Rac (Aref/A)^alpha sqrt(fac), Rflow (Aref/A)^beta}), and the pressure a narrowing's jet recovers past it. The acoustic term fitted by grid search to sixteen 3D-printed vowel resonators' measured bandwidths (hard walls, the glottis closed): the least error, 4.75 Hz on average, with fac the frequency itself, the law the passive core's fitted law keeps (src/v24/passive.rs fitted_scale); 2250 Hz the best single frequency, as 2.4's time-domain network takes it (14.5 Hz). The flow term L. P. Fulcher, R. C. Scherer & T. Powell's (2013, "Viscous effects in a static physical model of the uniform glottis", JASA 134(2), 1253-1260), held fixed; the recovery coefficients fitted to five printed glottises' pressure-flow relations. All seven their Table 2's row 4, the values they recommend, and VocalTractLab 2.4's Constants.h.

glottisRecovery.unit: of the jet's dynamic pressure, in the glottis

tractRecovery.unit: of the jet's dynamic pressure, above it

free.about: The parameters a fit may move (src/fitting.rs, vtl-fit fit), each with its feasible range and that range's source: a fit reads its bounds here and nowhere else, and one that ends at a bound is a finding, reported, never adopted (research/MODEL_REFACTOR_PLAN.md, "The method", 1; research/VOCALWIND_FITS.md). None is a constant above: each acts through a switch whose default is the engine as it was.

surfaces.source: The viscous boundary layer's impedance from the law as it is -- the fitted law as Birkholz & Häsner 2026 fitted it to printed tubes of circular section, or Zwikker and Kosten's smooth wall (1: a real tract's surfaces lose no less) -- to twice it: printed tracts from MRI measure 1.12 to 1.67 times the printed tubes' bandwidths by kilohertz band (Birkholz, Blandin & Kürbis 2023, Table I), and Fant 1972 took twice a smooth wall's surface loss for living tracts (S_A = 2, "adopted for all calculations"). A bound from those spans, not a measurement of the factor.

anatomy.about: The static ducts' sizes where nothing else gives them: the trachea's length, the nose's (which scales its area function), the piriform fossa's length and volume (VocalTractLab 2.4's Tube.h, as 2.3's Tube.cpp; their sources not stated there).
